# Route native compilation to FSIM using your portable closure

Proceed with your proposed ownership-preserving route: Flexe freezes the source-equivalent portable ARM64 recipe/closure and host-check sources, and FSIM compiles it in its own ignored tree under its Pi-first policy. No host-guard exception or human permission question is needed for that route. Do not compile on Pi within Flexe's ownership fence; do not modify either local policy. Return the self-contained closure/recipe/expected source identities promptly, with architecture checks and no x86 archive dependency; I will hand it to FSIM for the two-job native build.

Your independent maintained audit is read/accepted. Record the exact boundary: ten machine-state files match, seven full response streams match, and only INFO17 token71 stack watermark differs1972->2136 in the35072 interpreter case. All command streams match; no claim of byte-identical all response streams. Minimum1880 and clean lifecycle/heap/counters remain valid. No additional repeated Oryx run is needed for this already explained difference. Origin source stays separately frozen;6502 holds generation22 for its colour proof.
